ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 75:25 ratio of high-intensity white to low-intensity black/dark-gray pixels across the visible ventral surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant contiguous high-intensity white regions occupy the central areas of both lobes, bifurcated by a dark vertical band at the peduncle. Low-intensity black pigment forms a continuous border along the trailing edge and distal tips, with significant dark linear streaks and amorphous mottling distributed across the white fields.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 52 degrees and a bounding-box depth relative to the lobe peaks of roughly 15% of total fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Irregular serration profile; high-amplitude, low-frequency jagged peaks are concentrated at the distal tips, transitioning to high-frequency, low-amplitude micro-serrations along the mid-lobe trailing edge, and smoothing toward the median notch.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave upward sweep along the trailing edge from the notch to the tips; the leading edge exhibits a primary convex curvature.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Localized clusters of small, circular low-intensity spots on the lower right lobe; high-contrast white circular spots (rosettes) are visible against the black pigmentation of the distal tips.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Extensive network of dark, unaligned linear pixel disruptions. Multiple parallel groupings (3-5 lines per set) indicative of rake marks are visible diagonally on the left lobe and vertically/diagonally on the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent predatory rake marks across both lobes; irregular jagged morphology on the distal trailing edge of the right lobe suggesting previous tissue loss.
other_distinctive_markers: Dense, high-contrast vertical striations emanating from the insertion point of the peduncle, fanning out into the lower central region of the fluke.
